5. **Deutsches Textarchiv (DTA)** — screened and deferred. The current automated access path was blocked by robots/access policy in this environment; the cycle did not bypass it. Its scholarly historical-language value remains distinct from today's ordinary-reader task.

### Passing integration: Projekt Gutenberg-DE German Classics Discovery Starter

Projekt Gutenberg's current first-party site offers German-language classical literature as readable/searchable text and, since its June 2026 update, direct EPUB downloads. The current project also states that it has operated under new responsibility since 2026-01-01.

The rights boundary is deliberately conservative. Current first-party terms say that literary works are provided as public domain to the site's best knowledge while limiting use of the texts supplied on the website to private use and restricting broader reproduction, redistribution, publication, adaptation, or other use. Editorial preparation, structure, explanatory material, metadata, and design are separately protected unless otherwise stated. WebNR therefore does **not** treat the public-domain status of an underlying literary work as permission to republish the site's particular digital text or EPUB edition.

WebNR admits exactly three first-party link-only routes:

- `https://projekt-gutenberg.org/` — current reading/discovery entry point;
- `https://projekt-gutenberg.org/bibliothek/` — first-party A-Z work catalogue;
- `https://projekt-gutenberg.org/nutzungsbedingungen/` — current first-party use/reuse boundary.

The maintained source stores only those URLs plus WebNR-authored labels/descriptions and `Link-only-WebNR-editorial` markers. It adds no runtime Projekt Gutenberg search, chapter scraping, full-text extraction, EPUB download, metadata harvest, proxy, credential forwarding, or background synchronization. A future richer adapter remains gated on explicit automated-use permission plus stable record/file identity, browser transport, update/deletion, pagination, resource/failure limits, encoding, provenance/attribution, and versioned fixtures.

Maintained source families therefore increase from **33 to 34**. `Web Novel Discussion Radar Starter` remains unchanged at **12** link-only routes.

## Reader-content decision and September 20 guide

The September 18 Italian digital-library guide reached the repository's rolling 48-hour substantial-reader-content boundary during this cycle. A new practical reader asset was therefore warranted rather than cadence-only filler.

The published guide is **“德语免费经典电子书去哪找？Projekt Gutenberg、DDB、BSB 怎么选”**. It answers a concrete reader task: where to find German classics for immediate reading/EPUB, cross-institution discovery, and historical scans/IIIF, and how to distinguish free access, public-domain status, downloadable files, and permission to republish a site's digital edition. It compares Projekt Gutenberg, DDB, BSB/MDZ, Zeno.org, and DTA using current first-party evidence, links the newly admitted link-only starter, and keeps internal audit/CI/provider bookkeeping out of the reader-facing article.

No new top-level navigation or archive/category sprawl was introduced. The existing curated Blog hub received only two narrow links to the new guide: one in the legal-free-classics reader route and one at the top of the existing import/compatibility/source task table.

## Same-cycle production-evidence repair — pull request #184

The first closeout Quality run `35525070328` exposed a reproducible verification defect. Its application and GitHub Pages documentation-mirror checks observed the exact #182 build identity, and canonical `www` also returned the exact #182 `build.json`; however, the canonical documentation content check retried 42 times and failed because `scripts/verify-production-builds.mjs` still required `feed_rss_created.xml` to contain the hard-coded 2026-08-10 English-platform article. The bounded generated RSS had legitimately advanced and no longer retained that old entry. A rerun reproduced the same failure against the same current RSS ETag, ruling out ordinary propagation delay.

The repository's documentation Quality logic already verifies bounded RSS semantically by deriving the newest dated file under `docs/blog/posts`. Pull request #184, **“Fix bounded RSS production verification”**, applied the same bounded-feed invariant to public production evidence rather than weakening or skipping the check:

- preserve the established August 10 article page/canonical check as an unaffected representative surface;
- derive the lexically newest dated reader post from `docs/blog/posts` deterministically;
- require that newest reader URL to load canonically on `www` and to appear in both the canonical sitemap and bounded RSS;
- preserve exact `build.json` commit matching, DNS/public-origin verification, all content checks, retry budget, and analytics assertions;
- make no reader runtime, source payload, content, RSS generator, sitemap generator, analytics, route-layout, deployment-configuration, or source-capability change.

The exact final #184 head `c57a8de434f149603da0857a671f6a6d79664799` passed Quality run `35526114510`: Production evidence, Documentation quality, Web quality, and Chromium user journeys were all successful. Crucially, Production evidence immediately verified the then-current #182 application, GitHub Pages mirror, and canonical Cloudflare build identities and confirmed the September 20 German guide on canonical HTML, sitemap, and the same bounded RSS that the stale hard-coded assertion had rejected. After green CI, review restarted from the original operating contract and rechecked current main/base, the full two-file diff, both commits, unchanged pinned skill submodule, comments/reviews/threads, exact public evidence, and rollback scope; no finding remained.

Pull request #184 was exact-head squash-merged as `755a34ea1ee5cf4bced3df2921feb63f168d6524`. Post-merge main Quality run `35526351690` completed successfully: Production evidence, Documentation quality, Web quality, and Chromium user journeys all passed while the public surfaces still exposed their prior attributable targets.

Cloudflare's Git integration then completed `Cloudflare Pages: webnr-docs` check run `106119472086` for the exact #184 merge commit and reported a successful canonical documentation deployment. No application deployment or GitHub Pages documentation-mirror rebuild accompanied #184. Therefore the durable production state correctly becomes split: application and GitHub Pages mirror remain attributable to #182 (`4c26b0c1da74c7201d45c7dbe2f32aba68847635`), while canonical Cloudflare documentation advances to exact #184 merge commit `755a34ea1ee5cf4bced3df2921feb63f168d6524`. The closeout status was updated to that provider-attributable identity rather than forcing all three surfaces to share one commit.
